Exercise A – Complete using the correct form of the words in the box
Topic vocabulary in contrast. Choose the correct word from the box for each gap.
Word groups: prefect / pupil / student  |  achieve / reach  |  teach / learn  |  high / primary / secondary  |  degree / certificate / results
  • 1. In our school, most classes have about 35 in them.
    ✓ pupils (school children are pupils)
  • 2. Every year, two new are chosen from the best students in each class.
    ✓ prefects (senior pupils given responsibilities)
  • 3. The university accepts around 2000 new every year.
    ✓ students (university learners are students)
  • 4. When he finally graduated, Victor felt he had everything he set out to do.
    ✓ achieved (achieve = successfully complete goals)
  • 5. The work we're doing now will make more sense when you the sixth form.
    ✓ reach (reach = arrive at a point/level)
  • 6. Who you how to play the drums like that?
    ✓ taught (teach = give instruction to someone)
  • 7. I would love to a new language I don't know anything about, like Swedish.
    ✓ learn (learn = acquire knowledge)
  • 8. Children in England go to school from the ages of five to eleven.
    ✓ primary (primary school = ages 5–11)
  • 9. In Britain, grammar schools, public schools and comprehensives are often referred to as schools.
    ✓ secondary (secondary school = ages 11–18)
  • 10. Americans usually refer to their secondary school as a school, and there are often separate junior and senior schools.
    ✓ high (high school = US secondary school)
  • 11. The exam come out today and I'm really nervous. I hope I've passed.
    ✓ results (exam results = marks/grades)
  • 12. I was so proud when my exam finally arrived in the post.
    ✓ certificate (official document showing you passed)
  • 13. I would prefer to go to university and do a in astronomy, rather than start work.
    ✓ degree (university qualification)

Exercise C – Write one word in each gap
Phrasal verbs. Write one word to complete each phrasal verb.
  • 1. Just get with Exercise C and I'll be back in a minute.
    ✓ on (get on with = continue doing)
  • 2. My teacher says that I should sail the exam, but I'm not so sure.
    ✓ through (sail through = pass easily)

    ✓ at (getting at = trying to say/mean)
  • 4. We all tried to convince our teacher to change his mind about the school trip and he finally came .
    ✓ round / around (came round = changed his mind)

Exercise D – Sentence transformation (phrasal verbs)
Complete each second sentence using the word given so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words in each gap.
  • 1. The ideas in your essay need to be organised better. SET
    You need to in your essay better.

    You'll never pass the exam if you just like that.

    Nick just couldn't at university.

  • 5. I suddenly realised that I had left my homework at home. DAWNED
    It that I had left my homework at home.

  • 6. Ed was very lonely at university and he left after only one month. OUT
    Ed because he was very lonely.
    ✓ dropped out after only one month (drop out = leave before finishing)

  • 7. Mrs Dawson said that we are ………… our lesson in the library next Monday.

  • 8. In English yesterday, we had a discussion ………… different cultures.

  • 9. ………… my opinion, maths shouldn't be a compulsory subject.
    ✓ D In (In my opinion)
  • 10. When you ………… the exam tomorrow, try to stay calm and relaxed.
    ✓ C take (take an exam)

  • 14. I hadn't studied, so when the teacher asked me I had ………… idea.

Exercise F – Word patterns
Each of the words in bold is incorrect. Rewrite them correctly in the space provided.
  • 1. I've always admired our music teacher from being so patient.
    ✓ for (admire someone for something)
  • 2. My new school is quite similar with my old one.
    ✓ to (similar to)
  • 3. Mr Wilkins congratulated me for passing the exam.
    ✓ on (congratulate someone on something)
  • 4. I'd better go home and study on tomorrow's test.
    ✓ for (study for a test)
  • 5. Ian is capable for doing very well this year if he works hard.
    ✓ of (capable of doing)
  • 6. This course is suitable to students who are considering a career in the media.
    ✓ for (suitable for)
  • 7. If you don't get into university, you'll have to settle with art college.
    ✓ for (settle for = accept something less)
  • 8. After six attempts, Bill finally succeeded with passing his driving test.
    ✓ in (succeed in doing)
